# Karzoun KernWatch v0.1.0

KernWatch v0.1.0 is the first runtime-proven telemetry foundation for the project.

## What is included

- CO-RE eBPF build using the running kernel BTF
- libbpf skeleton generation and C userspace loader
- BPF ring-buffer transport
- process execution and process-exit observation
- outbound IPv4/IPv6 `connect(2)` attempt telemetry
- `openat(2)` attempt telemetry with bounded pathname capture
- kernel-side PID/UID filtering and userspace command-name filtering
- NDJSON schema-1 output
- per-CPU ring-buffer reserve-failure accounting
- graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown
- strict compiler warnings, userspace unit tests, ASan/UBSan and CodeQL
- privileged Ubuntu 24.04 runtime smoke proving real BPF load/attach plus exec/connect telemetry

## Important boundaries

KernWatch v0.1.0 is telemetry-only. It is not an EDR, anti-malware product, or policy-enforcement engine. Syscall-entry observations do not prove the underlying operation succeeded.

The repository and userspace source are Apache-2.0. The kernel BPF source in `bpf/kernwatch.bpf.c` is GPL-2.0-only because the tracing path uses Linux BPF helpers restricted to GPL-compatible programs.

## Distribution

v0.1.0 intentionally ships a source bundle plus SHA256 checksum rather than a prebuilt combined executable. The generated libbpf skeleton embeds the GPL-2.0-only BPF object into the userspace executable, so binary packaging is deferred until that distribution boundary is reviewed explicitly.

Build requirements and runtime constraints are documented in the README. A compatible Linux host must expose kernel BTF and allow BPF load/attach under its privilege and security policy.
